Definition: a deep place (of water or mud)
BiblicalUsage: The depths covered Pharaoh's army, Leviathan makes the deep boil like a pot, Jonah was cast into the deep in the midst of the seas, and God promises to cast all our sins into the depths of the sea. The word is the deep place itself, and Scripture moves from the sea that drowns armies to the sea that drowns sins.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Micah 7:19 is the verse that turns this word into gospel: the same depths that swallowed Pharaoh's host swallow our iniquities, and God casts them where no man can fish them out again. God casts our sins where no man can fish them out again.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea
